0.0.n: A standard daytime greeting, suitable for opening a video.

0.2.n: Sets the time frame for the lesson being introduced.

0.3.n: Marks 今日 as the topic of the introduction.

0.4.n: The name of the video game being discussed.

0.5.n: Links RimWorld to 初心者向け, identifying which game's beginners are intended.

0.6.n: 向け attaches to a group name to indicate the intended audience.

0.7.n: Connects 初心者向け to 講座, describing the course's intended audience.

0.8.n: Refers to instructional content, here a video guide.

0.9.n: Marks 講座 as the result with なる, though the phrase here simply introduces the video's format.

0.10.n: Polite form of なる; here it announces what today's video is rather than a literal change.

1.0.n: Introduces background information that may surprise the listener.

1.1.n: Past form of やる, a casual verb used here for playing a game.

1.2.n: After a past-form verb, こと helps express whether someone has ever done something.

1.3.n: With やったこと, it denies previous experience; casual speech leaves out が before ない.

1.4.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone before だ.

1.5.n: The plain linking word in んだ, completing the explanatory ending.

1.6.n: Connects the lack of previous experience to the recent start.

1.8.n: Gives the time of starting without needing a particle.

1.9.n: The て-form of 始める links this action to what follows.

1.11.n: The plain form before まで identifies the action marking the endpoint.

1.12.n: Sets starting the game as the endpoint of the preparation period.

1.13.n: Combines with まで to locate the difficulties in the period leading up to starting.

1.14.n: Refers to modifications or add-ons for the game.

1.15.n: Lists mods as one example among assorted complications.

1.16.n: A shortened form of なに; with やら, it vaguely refers to other unspecified things.

1.17.n: Completes なんやら, loosely referring to miscellaneous other things.

1.18.n: Marks mods and other complications as the reason starting was difficult.

1.19.n: The plain verb is followed by の so the action can serve as the subject.

1.20.n: Turns 始める into a noun-like expression that can be described as difficult.

1.21.n: Marks 始めるの as what was difficult.

1.22.n: Past form of 難しい, changing い to かった.

1.23.n: Adds an explanatory tone to the statement about past difficulty.

1.24.n: Adds emphasis to information the speaker is sharing.

1.25.n: Softens the statement and invites the listener to share the speaker's feeling.

2.0.n: The plain form describes the action associated with とき.

2.1.n: Follows a verb to identify the time of that action.

2.2.n: Marks 始めるとき as the time when the speaker encountered problems.

2.3.n: Past form of 困る, directly describing ところ.

2.4.n: Means aspects or parts here, not physical locations.

2.5.n: Lists troublesome points and things worth knowing as examples, without implying a complete list.

2.7.n: With に, it identifies when the speaker wishes they had known the information.

2.8.n: Turns 最初 into a time expression.

2.9.n: Refers broadly to information the speaker will introduce.

2.10.n: Marks これ as the information the speaker wishes they had known.

2.11.n: 知っておく means knowing in advance; おけばよかった expresses regret that this preparation did not happen.

2.12.n: Links the preceding thought to こと, describing the kind of things being introduced.

2.13.n: Refers to pieces of information described by the preceding wish.

2.14.n: Marks the listed points and information as what the speaker will introduce.

2.15.n: 紹介する becomes 紹介していこう, expressing an intention to proceed with introducing things.

2.16.n: Marks the preceding intention as the content of 思う.

2.17.n: After a form like いこう plus と, 思う expresses the speaker's plan.

2.18.n: A strongly casual, assertive ending, often masculine in tone.

0.lit: Hello, as for today, it will be a lesson aimed at RimWorld beginners.
0.tip: になります politely introduces what the video will be; it need not describe an actual transformation.

1.lit: Actually, I'd never played, but recently started; before starting, mods and whatnot made getting started difficult, you know.
1.tip: A past-form verb plus ことない means never having done that action before.

2.lit: I intend to introduce points I struggled with when starting and things I wish I'd known at the beginning.
2.tip: 〜ておけばよかった expresses wishing you had done something beforehand.
